> The **Repeat** option should be hidden in the inspector when using the conic gradient mode, as they have no effect no matter the from/to positions. You can do this by adding `GradientTexture2D::_validate_property()`, similar to the existing method in the Gradient class. Then call `notify_property_list_changed();` at the end of `GradientTexture2D::set_fill()`.

Actually it could make sense to implement as `ofs %= last_color_stop_position`, so if you have colors set to up to 25% of the gradient it would behave as if you repeated them 4 times in the `[0.25, 1]` range.
It's slightly different from repeat in the other modes, but the only way I can think of to make it consistent (which would also reusing gradients between different modes) would be to leave color stops as-is and make the number of repetitions (inverse, so closer together is more repetitions like in the other modes) magnitude of `(fill_to - fill_from)` which sounds very unintuitive, but maybe it could work if the gizmo changes to control them separately when it's selected? To illustrate what I mean:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f73a3cbe-1c2e-4065-a25c-fb149890607f

For reference CSS has [repeating-conic-gradient](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/gradient/repeating-conic-gradient).






> I don't see that particular CI failure in the log anymore. I could only see the one I linked above.

Nvm, it's [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/actions/runs/16397615231/job/46343696489?pr=108790#step:14:1986), I saw ["cc1plus: all warnings being treated as errors"](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/actions/runs/16397615231/job/46343696489?pr=108790#step:14:2101) and assumed it was considered an error because I could find the actual error, the github UI for CI logs is awful.

You can use `werror=yes` locally to turn warnings into errors, or use `dev_mode=yes` which is an alias for several development-related flags.

> the github UI for CI logs is awful.

We should be able to surface warnings/errors as annotations to C++ files that appear on the web interface. GitHub Actions has a way to make it possible but I didn't look into it yet. This way, you don't need to comb through logs anymore.
